plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay only that second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated interaction to exploit, the safest and most profit-maximizing action is to bid exactly my private value of $20.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. My value for this item is $0, meaning I have nothing to gain from winning - I would only lose money if I won since I'd have to pay whatever the second-highest bid is while gaining $0 in value. Therefore, I should bid exactly $0 to avoid any risk of winning and losing money.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders, since you pay the second-highest bid rather than your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a price above your value, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $24, so I will bid exactly that.
